title: HIGHWAY INFRASTRUCTURE FINANCING AND INVESTMENT
body_text:
Government in Ministry of Road Transport and Highways is primarily responsible for development and maintenance of National Highways (NHs). The Government has inter-alia decided to focus on development of Access controlled National High Speed Corridors (HSCs) / Expressways, development of ring road / bypasses of cities with population of more than One Lakh with priority on those cities which have population of more than Five Lakh, development of coastal roads, connectivity of ports as per the prioritization of Ministry of Shipping, Ports and Waterways, connectivity of airports as per the prioritization of Ministry of Civil Aviation and connectivity to Industrial nodes as per the priority of National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC) for improving the logistics efficiency of the country. These steps are directed towards broadening investment opportunities in highway infrastructure.
To attract more private players and make investment opportunities more attractive, the Government has taken several initiatives like reforms in Model Concession Agreement for Public Private Partnership (PPP) Projects, reforms in model contracts for monetization of NHs through Toll Operate and Transfer (TOT) basis, introduction of Public InvIT to widen investment scope, Stakeholder Conferences held with concessionaires, financiers, and major government bodies to showcase investment opportunities to private players as well as understand & address investors' concerns etc.
Major amendments in the standard bidding and concession documents for Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) projects on NHs include: -
Enhanced bidder eligibility by permitting participation of Fund Houses on their financial strength. Upon successful award of project, they shall engage EPC contractors possessing the requisite technical experience for execution of the works. Learning from past litigations and contractual interpretations and for greater contractual clarity; provisions relating to Change in Ownership, Target Traffic, Damages, Compensation for Breach of Agreement, Compensation for Force Majeure Costs, Payment of Construction Support during the Construction Period in Capacity Augmentation projects, Compensation for Annual Passes, and Change of Scope have been amended. Provision for payment of Termination Compensation before the Commercial Operation Date (COD) where the physical progress of the project is 20% or more, thereby protecting the interests of both the Concessionaire and the lenders. Streamlined provisions relating to the determination of Debt Due to remove ambiguities and provide greater certainty in their application. Streamlined Dispute Resolution mechanism – Dispute Resolution Board abolished; Disputes less than ₹ 10 Cr to be resolved through Arbitration and Disputes of ₹ 10 Cr and above through Conciliation or Mediation.
This information was given by Union Minister of Road Transport & Highways, Shri Nitin Gadkari in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.
***
GDH/DS/HJ

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways has outlined its strategy to boost highway infrastructure financing by prioritizing access-controlled expressways, ring roads/bypasses for cities above one lakh population, coastal roads, and connectivity to ports, airports and industrial nodes. To attract private investment, it has reformed Model Concession Agreements, Toll Operate and Transfer (TOT) contracts, introduced Public InvIT, and amended BOT bidding/concession documents covering eligibility, dispute resolution, and compensation provisions. This was stated by Union Minister Nitin Gadkari in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha on 12 August 2026.
enrichment.context:
Highway development in India has increasingly relied on PPP models like BOT, Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM), and TOT to supplement budgetary resources, given the scale of investment needed for the Bharatmala Pariyojana and other national highway expansion programs. Reforms such as InvITs (Infrastructure Investment Trusts) allow monetization of operational highway assets, freeing up capital for new construction while giving institutional investors access to steady toll-based returns. The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) launched India's first Public InvIT to broaden the investor base beyond traditional infrastructure funds.

The amendments to Model Concession Agreements reflect lessons learned from past disputes between concessionaires, lenders, and NHAI, particularly around termination compensation, force majeure, and change of scope—issues that had previously led to prolonged litigation and stalled projects. The shift from a Dispute Resolution Board to arbitration (for smaller disputes) and conciliation/mediation (for larger ones) aims to reduce delays and legal costs, aligning with the broader ease-of-doing-business agenda. These reforms are also connected to India's Gati Shakti National Master Plan, which emphasizes multimodal connectivity integrating highways with ports, airports, and industrial corridors for improved logistics efficiency and reduced logistics costs as a share of GDP.

GS Paper 2 - Governance: Contract and dispute resolution reforms
GS Paper 3 - Economy: Logistics and multimodal connectivity (Gati Shakti)

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following is a mechanism used by the Government of India to monetize existing operational National Highways by transferring toll collection rights to private entities for a fixed period?
prelims_questions.explanation: Toll Operate and Transfer (TOT) is the model by which NHAI monetizes operational national highways by auctioning toll collection rights to private concessionaires for a fixed concession period, generating upfront revenue for new highway construction.

prelims_questions.question: As per the recent reforms mentioned by the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways, disputes of what value under BOT concession agreements are to be resolved through Arbitration?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the reforms, disputes below ₹10 Crore are to be resolved through Arbitration, while disputes of ₹10 Crore and above are to be resolved through Conciliation or Mediation, following the abolition of the Dispute Resolution Board.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of Public-Private Partnership (PPP) models such as BOT, HAM, and TOT in financing India's national highway infrastructure. Examine the recent reforms undertaken by the Government to make these models more attractive to private investors.
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 3 - Economy: Infrastructure and Investment

mains_questions.question: Efficient dispute resolution mechanisms are critical to sustaining private investment in infrastructure projects. In light of recent amendments to highway concession agreements, discuss the challenges in the earlier dispute resolution framework and how the new mechanism addresses them.
